en.topic_title: Taiwan’s ageing seaweed harvesters hope younger women wade in to keep tradition alive
en.topic_summary:
By Joy Chiang and Sally Jensen



Unfazed by the crashing waves, 72-year-old Wu Feng-chiao yanks fistfuls of brownish-purple seaweed she will process into jelly, one of the last women in Taiwan keeping the marine harvest tradition alive.



Wu Feng-chiao, 72, carries a freshly harvested load of gelidium algae, locally known as “stone flowers”, along Taiwan’s northeastern coast in Magang fishing village in New Taipei City on June 16, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng/AFP.
